eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus has locked onto a 27 °C maximum for Hong Kong on May 15 because official Hong Kong Observatory data recorded precisely that peak under persistent overcast skies, 83–89 % relative humidity, and widespread thundery showers driven by a low-pressure trough. Mid-May subtropical climatology normally supports gradual warming toward 29–31 °C as the southwest monsoon strengthens, yet the trough suppressed solar heating and promoted convective cooling, keeping daytime highs firmly capped. This outcome aligns with historical analogs for trough-dominated days, where maximum temperatures rarely exceed the mid-20s. Clearer anticyclonic conditions or a delayed trough passage could have allowed readings to reach 29 °C or higher, but the verified station data removed remaining uncertainty and anchored market-implied odds near certainty.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 18 May '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts for Manila on May 18 point to partly cloudy conditions under the influence of the prevailing easterly flow and high-pressure ridge, supporting a peak temperature near the seasonal climatological average of 34°C. PAGASA guidance and ensemble model runs show limited cloud development and light winds that favor afternoon heating without significant convective suppression, placing 34°C as the modal outcome while keeping 33°C and 35°C within realistic model spread. Recent observations from the Ninoy Aquino International Airport station confirm similar daily maxima in the preceding week amid persistent hot-season humidity, with no strong signals for either a pronounced heat spike or widespread afternoon storms that would cap temperatures below 34°C. Traders are therefore weighting the narrow 33–35°C range most heavily as resolution nears.
